Regression from #111384 , which added an error message when viewport is not set. Should be benign.

I'll see if this can be fixed in the calling code from the physics interpolation.

Actually, this is caused simply by calling `Camera2D::get_camera_transform()` (presumably when `viewport` hasn't been set). I suspect this should be able to be called without flagging an error, might need a look by @harperstoeckle .

I *can* fix it in the calling code, but I'm not sure whether it flagging an error here is correct, and would like to at least have that confirmed.

Effectively to fix it on the calling side I'd have to add presumably some conditions before calling `get_camera_transform()` each time, just in case it isn't valid .. and that kind of sounds kind of difficult to maintain, and like the error checking is in the wrong place, and maybe just returning an identity xform without an error message might be a better way (or reverting to the old behaviour in this case?).

This problem seems to occur because `NOTIFICATION_RESET_PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION` is sent by `CanvasItem` when it receives `NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE` (i.e., before `NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE` can finish going down through every derived class). This means that `Camera2D` receives `NOTIFICATION_RESET_PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION` *after* it has entered the tree, but *before* it has received `NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE`, which is where it initializes `viewport`. I'm not sure if there's a great way to fix that ordering, but it seems like a bit of an issue that nodes can't rely on being fully initialized in this case.

Since all of the data necessary to set `viewport` is already available at the time `NOTIFICATION_RESET_PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION` is received, it feels like the "most correct" solution is to introduce some sort of `_update_viewport` function that can be used to update the cached viewport before any calls to `get_camera_transform` that might happen in that dubious half-initialized state. I guess the other option is to directly update it in `get_camera_transform` and either make `get_camera_transform` non-const or make `viewport` mutable, but both of those seem like bad form to me.

Defaulting to an identity transform when `viewport` isn't set would definitely fix the error, but it would mean that the wrong transform would be used for calculating the interpolation data when the camera is first added to the tree. I don't know enough about physics interpolation to know whether that would be a problem.
That's a good assessment, I'll try and have a look later and figure the best option. 👍

I've had a look - it turns out I was aware of the problem, and there is an existing manual reset at the end of `Camera2D::NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE`, so this is purely cosmetic.

I've done a simple PR above just to limit the resets to inside the `ENTER / EXIT TREE` lifetime, hopefully this should be enough to do the job, and keep a local solution.
